title: Intelligent teaching design assistant for primary mathematics: A large language model-driven framework with retrieval-augmented generation and problem-chain pedagogy
venue: International Electronic Journal of Mathematics Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem that primary mathematics teachers face substantial cognitive overload and weak support when designing lesson plans, especially under curriculum reform pressures. The authors argue that general-purpose large language models can help with lesson planning, but that they often produce generic, context-insensitive, and sometimes inaccurate outputs that are not well aligned to curriculum standards, student characteristics, or pedagogical goals.

To address this, the study develops an Intelligent Teaching Design Assistant built on large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and a multi-agent architecture. The system draws on three knowledge bases: curriculum standards, teaching strategies, and student profiles. It also includes a process planner and student simulator to support problem-chain pedagogy and make the design process more transparent and teacher-facing. The intervention was tested with 34 elementary school mathematics teachers in China, who used the tool to design a lesson on multiplying decimals by whole numbers and compared it with a generic large language model condition.

The results showed that the assistant improved lesson-plan quality across all evaluated dimensions, with especially strong gains in teaching objectives, analysis of teaching situation and textbook content, problem-chain design, usability, and overall ratings. Teachers also reported high ease of use, perceived usefulness, acceptance, and satisfaction. The paper concludes that pedagogically grounded generative AI can function as a teacher-facing cognitive partner for lesson planning, though it still needs better support for interdisciplinary knowledge integration and formative assessment design.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based generative AI chatbot and language model family used for conversational text generation and assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the generic large language model in the control condition for lesson design, and also mentioned in the paper’s AI statement as a writing/readability aid during manuscript preparation.

findings.finding_summary: In the control condition, teachers used a general-purpose large language model via its standard web interface to create a lesson plan for 'Multiplying Decimals by Whole Numbers.' Compared with the purpose-built assistant, the generic model produced significantly lower-quality lesson designs across all evaluated dimensions; the overall rating was M=3.67 for Task 1 versus M=5.83 for Task 2 (p<0.01).
findings.measure: Lesson plan quality / instructional design evaluation

quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental comparative study with 34 teachers and rated lesson-plan outputs, plus post-use survey data. It is empirical and reasonably designed, but not randomized and without reported effect sizes or full assumption checks.
impact_tier_rationale: The comparison shows statistically significant improvement in lesson-plan quality, but the paper does not report standardized effect sizes. The practical gains are clear, yet the absence of effect-size reporting makes the magnitude harder to classify precisely.
